> **What this case shows** — the complexity of a brain signal — how unpredictable its
> moment-to-moment fluctuations are — is a workhorse biomarker: **permutation entropy**
> tracks cortical state, depth of anaesthesia, consciousness, and neurological disease.
> But complexity measures are notorious for implementation-dependent definitions.
> Permutation entropy (Bandt & Pompe 2002) is the exception: it counts the signal's
> **ordinal (rank) patterns** and takes the normalized Shannon entropy of their
> distribution — an *exactly-defined* algorithm. Running `eegComplexity` on all **64
> channels** of a real eyes-closed resting EEG and comparing, channel by channel,
> against the canonical Python **antropy** shows they agree not approximately but to
> **machine precision**: the per-channel entropies correlate **1.0** with a maximum
> absolute difference of **2×10⁻¹⁶**, and the values are physiologically plausible
> (mean 0.91). **The complexity biomarker the ecosystem reports is, to the last bit,
> the field-standard one.**

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — to quantify signal complexity: take the EEG → call
`eegComplexity(pe, measures="permutation_entropy", perm_order, tau)` → read the
per-channel entropy → map it as a complexity biomarker (topography, state contrast).
**Way of thinking** — not all complexity measures are equal: permutation entropy is
*exactly defined* (ordinal patterns), so it is reproducible to the bit; sample entropy
(a tolerance `r`) and spectral entropy (a PSD estimate) carry implementation choices,
so cross-tool numbers differ — always know which kind you are reporting.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioEEG::eegComplexity()` offers permutation / sample /
approximate / multiscale entropy, Lempel-Ziv, Higuchi FD, DFA, Hjorth, and spectral
entropy.
:::

## Proposition

On all 64 channels of a real eyes-closed resting EEG (eegmmidb S001R02),
`eegComplexity`'s permutation entropy reproduces the canonical Python `antropy` to
machine precision: correlation 1.0, max |diff| = 2×10⁻¹⁶, mean entropy 0.91.

## Question & goal

**The question is whether the ecosystem's complexity number is the field-standard
number.** A biomarker is only comparable across studies if the computation is the
same. The goal is a channel-by-channel head-to-head against `antropy`, choosing a
measure — permutation entropy — that is exactly defined so that any difference would
be a genuine implementation bug, not a convention.

## Challenge & approach

Complexity measures hide implementation choices. We sidestep them by validating the
one measure with no free tolerance: permutation entropy of order 3, delay 1. We
compute it per channel with `eegComplexity` and with `antropy.perm_entropy`, matched
settings, and compare.

```
readEDF → eegComplexity (permutation entropy, per channel) ┐
                                                           ├─ compare → r, max|diff|
same signal → antropy.perm_entropy (order 3, delay 1)      ┘
```

## Data

**eegmmidb — EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (PhysioNet)**: subject S001, baseline
run **R02 (eyes-closed rest)**, all 64 channels, 160 Hz. The same EDF the sibling
`eeg-aperiodic` / `eeg-berger` cases read. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: the permutation entropy of each of the 64 channels — eegComplexity versus the canonical antropy, on the dashed identity line (r = 1.0, max |diff| = 2×10⁻¹⁶: the points are indistinguishable from the line). Right: the per-channel complexity across the scalp (mean 0.91, range 0.74–0.98) — a plausible resting-EEG complexity topography.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* if the two tools disagreed at all, the left panel would show
scatter off the diagonal. Instead every point lies exactly on it — the two
implementations of permutation entropy are numerically identical.

| Quantity | This reproduction | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Entropy correlation (64 ch) | **1.0** | `antropy` |
| Max \|entropy diff\| | **2×10⁻¹⁶** | 0 (identical algorithm) |
| Mean permutation entropy | **0.908** | **0.908** (antropy) |
| Channels | **64** | — |

The two engines are numerically identical across the head. Values trace to
[`artifacts/perm_entropy_summary.csv`](artifacts/perm_entropy_summary.csv) and the
per-channel table
[`artifacts/perm_entropy_by_channel.csv`](artifacts/perm_entropy_by_channel.csv).

## Conclusion

The ecosystem's permutation entropy is exactly the field-standard `antropy` computation
— so the complexity biomarker it reports is bit-for-bit comparable to the literature.
The transferable takeaway: **prefer an exactly-defined complexity measure (permutation
entropy) when you need cross-study comparability, and validate it against the canonical
tool — tolerance-dependent measures like sample entropy will not match to the bit.**

## Open questions

- Permutation entropy is a per-channel scalar; its power as a biomarker comes from
  **contrasts** — eyes-open vs eyes-closed, across sleep stages, across the scalp as a
  complexity topography, or against a clinical group. Extending this validated
  estimator to a within-subject **state contrast** (does complexity drop when the eyes
  close?) or a **multiscale** version (Costa's MSE across time scales) would turn a
  validated number into a complexity study. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| signal complexity (permutation / sample / …) | `eegComplexity()` | PhysioEEG |
| the aperiodic 1/f background (context) | `eegAperiodic()` | PhysioEEG |
| band power (oscillatory context) | `bandPower()` | PhysioEEG |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **measure** — for cross-study comparability prefer `permutation_entropy` (exactly
  defined); reach for `sample_entropy` / `dfa` only when you fix and report their
  parameters, because they differ between tools.
- **perm_order / tau** — order 3–5 and delay 1 are standard; higher order needs more
  data (there are `order!` patterns to populate).
- **normalization** — keep it normalized (÷ log(order!)) so entropies are comparable
  across settings and channels.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioEEG)

pe <- readEDF("S001R02.edf")                            # 64-ch eyes-closed rest
cx <- eegComplexity(pe, measures = "permutation_entropy",
                    perm_order = 3, tau = 1)
cx$permutation_entropy                                   # per-channel complexity
mean(cx$permutation_entropy)                             # 0.908

# exact by construction: matches the canonical antropy.perm_entropy to machine precision
```
